Scenario title: Monitoring as a service: moving from selling autonomous crop-monitoring robots outright to offering continuous crop monitoring to greenhouse growers on subscription.
Market or domain: who today buy equipment outright and have no in-house data specialist.
Why this scenario why now: Catch crop stress and disease days earlier than a walk-through inspection does
Stage of decision: without hiring specialist staff to interpret the data.
column7: Greenhouse horticulture in the Netherlands and north-west Europe. Hardware margins are falling as competing robot platforms reach the market. Subscription monitoring exists in field agriculture but not under glass at this scale.
column8: Robot hardware has been proven at two pilot growers. Labor shortage makes manual inspection harder to staff each year. The detection model works but degrades without ongoing agronomic input
column9: and nobody currently pays for that input.
column10: Under active internal debate. Commitment to the existing equipment sales business is firm. Whether to go to market own-brand
column12: or white-label behind an existing platform is open.
